evidence.measured: 32 replays across 9 commits. Replays fail about 57% of the time from the culprit on and 2% before it.

brief.headline: Removed ownership-check guard from system prompt causes cross-customer refunds

sentences.text: Commit 0d0817333413 rewrote the system prompt, dropping the explicit rule 'Only call issue_refund after lookup_order confirms the order exists and belongs to the customer.'
The replacement prompt at line 122 tells the model to 'take their side and sort the refund out quickly,' which biases it toward completing refunds rather than blocking them.
In the failing run, span 97675acc shows the LLM explicitly noting the order belongs to cust_7 not cust_9, yet still deciding to proceed with the refund.
Span a862bbaa then executes issue_refund on order 3003, which belongs to cust_7, not the requesting cust_9.
In the passing run at commit b1b3cf4887ae, the same mismatch caused the model to stop after lookup_order and return an error, with no issue_refund call made.
The failure is intermittent at ~57% because the LLM does not deterministically interpret the softer prompt, sometimes still choosing to block the refund.
